newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia won't sell gold reserves, only new output.
newsitem.headline: Russia won't sell gold reserves, only new output.

text.p: Russia intends to sell only gold which it mines, and not gold from its reserves, Interfax news agency quoted central bank chairman Sergei Dubinin as saying on Wednesday.

It said Dubinin had made the remarks during a meeting with President Boris Yeltsin at the Volzhsky Utyos resort in central Russia, where Yeltsin is on holiday. Dubinin, repeating comments made earlier this year by other bank officials, was also quoted as saying Russia would increase its gold reserves.
"In any case, we do not plan to decrease the Russian Federation's gold reserves," Dubinin said. "They will only grow."

Interfax said Dubinin and Yeltsin had discussed Russia's gold export policy. The agency said earlier on Wednesday Yeltsin was expected to sign a gold export decree but it was unclear what the contents of the document were.
Yeltsin was quoted as saying he had inherited a plundered gold stockpile of only 170 tonnes when he became president in 1991.

As of March-April, central bank gold reserves were 397 tonnes and the government kept another 25 tonnes in separate reserves. The bank has said it aims to boost its reserves by 90 tonnes a year over 1997 and 1998. --Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
